questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of force is Newton (N), named after Sir Isaac Newton. 1 Newton = 1 kg?m/s?.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a good conductor of heat?
questions.explanation: Copper is a good conductor of heat. Wood, plastic and rubber are insulators.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the Earth approximately?
questions.explanation: The acceleration due to gravity on Earth's surface is approximately 9.8 m/s?, denoted by 'g'.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which law explains the conservation of energy in a closed system?
questions.explanation: The First Law of Thermodynamics states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed from one form to another.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the unit of power?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of power is Watt (W), named after James Watt. 1 Watt = 1 Joule per second.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the speed of light in vacuum approximately?
questions.explanation: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately 3 ? 10? m/s, which is the fastest speed in the universe.

questions.subject: General Science

questions.explanation: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate with chemical formula Na?CO??10H?O.

questions.subject: General Science

questions.explanation: Quicklime is chemically known as Calcium oxide (CaO).

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the pH of pure water at 25?C?
questions.explanation: The pH of pure water at 25?C is 7, which is neutral.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is the lightest gas?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is the lightest gas with molar mass 2 g/mol. Helium is the second lightest.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the number of protons in a carbon atom?
questions.explanation: Carbon has atomic number 6, which means it has 6 protons in its nucleus.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which element is used in pencil leads?
questions.explanation: Pencil leads are made of graphite, which is a form of carbon. Despite the name, they do not contain lead.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: Skin is the largest organ of the human body, covering the entire body and protecting it from the environment.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which gland controls the metabolic rate of the body?
questions.explanation: The thyroid gland secretes thyroxine, which regulates the body's metabolic rate.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which blood group is called the universal donor?
questions.explanation: O negative blood group is the universal donor as it lacks A, B and Rh antigens and can be given to anyone.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which vitamin is also known as ascorbic acid?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is also known as ascorbic acid. It is essential for the growth and repair of tissues.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the function of hemoglobin in the blood?
questions.explanation: Hemoglobin is the iron-containing protein in red blood cells that transports oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following is a disease caused by bacteria?
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Malaria is caused by a parasite, polio and influenza are viral diseases.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which part of the plant carries water from the roots to the leaves?
questions.explanation: Xylem tissue transports water and minerals from the roots to the leaves in plants.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which animal is known as the ship of the desert?
questions.explanation: Camel is known as the 'Ship of the Desert' because it can travel long distances in deserts without water for many days.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the unit of electrical resistance?
questions.explanation: The unit of electrical resistance is Ohm (?), named after German physicist Georg Simon Ohm.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which element is used in the treatment of water as a disinfectant?
questions.explanation: Chlorine is widely used as a disinfectant in water treatment to kill bacteria and other harmful microorganisms.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which organ in the human body stores bile?
questions.explanation: The gall bladder stores bile produced by the liver and releases it into the small intestine to aid in fat digestion.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the formula for power in terms of work and time?
questions.explanation: Power (P) is defined as the rate of doing work. Formula: P = Work / Time = W / t.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: What is the genetic material in the nucleus of a cell called?
questions.explanation: DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) is the genetic material present in the nucleus of a cell that carries hereditary information.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: A is the father of B. B is the sister of C. C is the son of D. How is D related to A?
questions.explanation: A is father of B and C (since B and C are siblings). C is son of D. So D is the mother of C, and hence wife of A.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Mohan starts from point A and walks 8 km towards East. He turns left and walks 6 km. He then turns left and walks 8 km. In which direction is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: Starts ? 8 km East ? turns left (North) 6 km ? turns left (West) 8 km. Net displacement = 6 km North. So he is in North direction.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Ravi walks 6 km towards South. He turns right and walks 8 km. He then turns right and walks 6 km. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: Starts 6 km South ? turns right (West) 8 km ? turns right (North) 6 km. Net displacement = 8 km West. So distance = 8 km.

questions.question: Statements: All flowers are beautiful. Some flowers are red. Conclusions: I. Some red things are beautiful. II. All red things are flowers. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: Some flowers are red and all flowers are beautiful ? Some red things are beautiful (I follows). But all red things may not be flowers (II does not follow).

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Statements: No pen is a book. All erasers are books. Conclusions: I. No eraser is a pen. II. Some pens are erasers. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: No pen is a book and all erasers are books ? No eraser is a pen (I follows). II contradicts I.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Pointing to a man in a photograph, a woman said, "He is the only son of my father's father." How is that man related to the woman?
questions.explanation: Father's father = Grandfather. His only son = the woman's father (since the woman's father is the only son of her grandfather). So the man is her father.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who was the first President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: W.C. Bonnerjee was the first President of the Indian National Congress at its first session in Bombay in 1885.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The famous 'Salt March' was started from which place?
questions.explanation: The Salt March (Dandi March) was started by Mahatma Gandhi from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930 to Dandi.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who was the first woman Governor of independent India?
questions.explanation: Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of independent India, serving as Governor of Uttar Pradesh from 1947 to 1949.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
questions.explanation: The President of India appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with Fundamental Duties?
questions.explanation: Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 and are described in Part IV-A (Article 51A) of the Constitution.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is elected by?
questions.explanation: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is elected by the members of the Lok Sabha from among themselves.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which state is the largest producer of wheat in India?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of wheat in India, followed by Punjab and Haryana.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The 'Golden Triangle' of India includes which three cities?
questions.explanation: The Golden Triangle of India is a tourist circuit connecting Delhi, Agra (Taj Mahal) and Jaipur (Pink City).

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The longest river in India is?
questions.explanation: The Ganga is the longest river in India with a length of about 2525 km. Brahmaputra is longer overall but mostly flows outside India.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The 'GST' was implemented in India on which date?
questions.explanation: Goods and Services Tax (GST) was implemented in India on 1 July 2017, replacing multiple indirect taxes.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which organization releases the 'World Economic Outlook' report?
questions.explanation: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) releases the 'World Economic Outlook' report twice a year.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which vitamin is known as 'Niacin'?
questions.explanation: Vitamin B3 is also known as Niacin. It is essential for the proper functioning of the nervous system and digestion.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which organ filters blood and produces urine in the human body?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter blood to remove waste products and produce urine. Each human has two kidneys.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which of the following is the hardest naturally occurring substance?
questions.explanation: Diamond is the hardest naturally occurring substance known, with a rating of 10 on the Mohs scale.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who wrote the famous book 'Godaan'?
questions.explanation: Godaan' is a famous Hindi novel written by Munshi Premchand, published in 1936. It is considered one of the finest works of Hindi literature.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The autobiography 'My Experiments with Truth' is written by?
questions.explanation: My Experiments with Truth' (original title: Satyana Prayogo athava Atmakatha) is the autobiography of Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who is known as the 'Flying Sikh' of India?
questions.explanation: Milkha Singh is known as the 'Flying Sikh' for his exceptional sprinting achievements, including his gold medal at the 1958 Commonwealth Games.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which Indian boxer won a bronze medal at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics?
questions.explanation: Lovlina Borgohain won a bronze medal in women's welterweight boxing at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which Indian classical dance form originates from the state of Kerala?
questions.explanation: Kathakali is a major form of classical Indian dance that originated in Kerala. It is known for its elaborate makeup and costumes.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which day is celebrated as 'World Environment Day'?
questions.explanation: World Environment Day is celebrated on 5 June every year. It was established by the United Nations in 1972.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Who is known as the 'Iron Man of India'?
questions.explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is known as the 'Iron Man of India' for his role in integrating the princely states into the Indian Union.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which constitutional body conducts elections in India?
questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body established under Article 324. It conducts all elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which river is known as the 'Life Line of Kerala'?
questions.explanation: Periyar is known as the 'Life Line of Kerala'. It is the longest river in Kerala and provides water for irrigation, drinking, and hydroelectric power.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: The apex bank of India is?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central bank and apex banking institution of India. It regulates the monetary policy and the banking system.

questions.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
questions.question: Which day is celebrated as 'World Ozone Day'?
questions.explanation: World Ozone Day is celebrated on 16 September every year to commemorate the signing of the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer in 1987.
